ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Statistical victims donate MORE contradicts the identifiable victim effect being replicated
ground_truth.original_snippet: meaning that participants who faced an identifiable victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the statistical victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).
ground_truth.modified_snippet: meaning that participants who faced a statistical victim (M=2.54, SD=1.76) tended to donate more than those who faced the identifiable victims (M=2.24, SD=1.67).
ground_truth.description: Reversed which condition has higher donations — IVE is now reversed (statistical > identifiable), contradicting the phenomenon being replicated and Table 11 descriptives

matched_finding.subcategory: sign of test statistic contradicts mean interpretation
matched_finding.description: The t statistic for identifiable versus statistical victims is negative, but the text interprets the comparison as identifiable victims receiving higher donations than statistical victims. The sign may depend on contrast coding, but the manuscript does not define the coding, and the table label implies the opposite direction. This creates ambiguity about the direction of the effect.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Says 'no exclusion' then lists exclusions — direct contradiction

matched_finding.description: The manuscript says no samples were excluded, but it does not report incomplete responses, dropout after random assignment, failed attention/comprehension checks, duplicate MTurk IDs, bot screening, or how missing item-level data would be handled. For online experiments, these omissions threaten internal validity and reproducibility.
matched_finding.quote: There was no exclusion of samples in this study.
